To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) unpredictable variation in food availability can have profound effects on the physiology and behavior of animals, and 2) these effects are independent of the actual energetic state of the animal.

birds fed varying amounts of food per day, compared to birds fed the same amount of food per day: (1) lost mass, (2) had higher circulating levels of corticosterone, (3) had higher levels of circulating vasotocin (a hypothalamic peptide that is released in response to stress), (4) had greater use of protein and fat energy stores, and (5) were more behaviorally restless.

birds fed a variable amount of food each day lost mass, increased their circulating levels of corticosterone, increased their use of fat and protein stores, and increased their behavioral activity, compared with birds fed the same amount of food daily.

understanding how variation in food availability influences the behavior and physiology of animals.
the behavioral, physiological and ecological responses of birds to unpredictable environments.
understanding the behavioral, physiological, and endocrine mechanisms that allow animals to cope with variation in their environment.
